status: Manufacturing now has a bounded native BOM/formula register read for one Company, an owner-local HTTP router, a strict Next transport, and a fail-closed SSR cutover on the Manufacturing workspace. The Manufacturing owner remains pending/partial: shared composition mounting, root workspace-member registration, specification/order/planning commands, production run, material readiness and quality disposition remain open.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice reads the current Company's manufacturing specifications with their component lines and ordered routing operations. It does not create, approve, reject, retire or freeze a specification; it does not read or write manufacturing orders, plans, reservations, production runs, posts, lots or quality dispositions. The other five Manufacturing workflows are not claimed.
scope.domain: BOM actor policy (`records.read` plus the Manufacturing module plus selected-context expiry), exact Company identity, bounded specification/line/operation counts, status/mode enums, positive quantities and batch size, 1..20000 expected yield, version/timestamp bounds, independent reviewer rules for reviewed states, unique specification/line/operation identifiers, unique component products and ordinals, material not equal to output, operation routing facts and exact owner row shape.
scope.application: One `bom_register` use case requires the current actor before any repository call, reads only the actor Company's specifications and validates every owner row before presentation.
scope.adapters: Own SQL over `manufacturing_specifications`, `manufacturing_specification_lines`, `manufacturing_specification_operations` and `production_resources`. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required. No Commerce, Inventory, Finance, Quality, Records, IAM mutation or other owner SQL is written or read. No owner write is performed.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/manufacturing/specifications. Exact Host/Holding targets, exact HTTPS origin validation, duplicate/unknown query rejection, private/no-store and no-referrer/nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company/branch/department scope, purchase admission and serializable owner read.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_MANUFACTURING_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact specification/line/operation shapes, unique IDs/products/ordinals, Company identity, independent reviewer state and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader.
scope.ssr: The Manufacturing workspace presenter uses the native register when `ERPX_NATIVE_MANUFACTURING_CONFIG` is present. The native rows replace the workspace specification list supplied to `ProductionConsole`, remain filtered by the retained per-record purchase history when package enforcement is active, and add a BOM/component/routing register section. Component and output labels come from the retained Commerce product list already loaded by `productionWorkspace`; missing labels fall back to the stable product identifier. An unset configuration retains the legacy specification list and page exactly; once configured, an invalid or failed native read is surfaced rather than silently replaced.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The Next owned wrapper keeps the retained Manufacturing module, `records.read` and `requireManufacturingPurchasedRead` (capability `manufacturing.bom`) preflight ahead of the native read. This is a preflight, not an atomic owner unit; the composition backend must repeat current authority, selected branch/department scope and purchase admission on its own serializable owner transaction.
scope.notClaimed: No specification command, CAS write, idempotency receipt, audit/outbox event, order/planning command, production run, material reservation, quality disposition, attachments command, shared composition mount, root workspace membership, browser journey, staging or production acceptance.
